title: OPSO responds to public speculation after local student remains in ICE custody - NewsBreak
text:
By Lexi Corum ,
11 hours ago
WEST MONROE, La. ( KTVE/KARD ) — On Wednesday, July 29, 2026, authorities with the Ouachita Parish Sheriff’s Office announced that officials with the Sheriff’s Office have recently partnered with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) during a targeted enforcement operation focused on identifying individuals who are unlawfully present in the United States.
They say one of the individuals targeted during this operation was 19-year-old Omar Monzon-Vasquez Anderson. In a statement released by the Ouachita Parish Sheriff’s Office, Anderson was described as “an illegal alien from Guatemala. According to ICE, Monzon unlawfully entered the United States in 2020 with his mother and was released pending immigration proceedings.”
Anderson’s case has attracted significant public speculation and attention on social media, as he was taken into custody by ICE agents on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, after being stopped and failing to present his Social Security card, which was not on his person at the time, despite showing other forms of identification. At this time, he is being held at the Richland Parish Detention Center.
The statement released by the Ouachita Parish Sheriff’s Office in regard to 19-year-old Omar Monzon-Vasquez Anderson reads: “On July 27, 2026, ICE states that Monzon attempted to purchase a rifle in West Monroe. Federal authorities allege that, as an individual unlawfully present in the United States, he is prohibited from possessing a firearm. ICE further alleges that Monzon falsely represented himself as a United States citizen during the attempted purchase, a violation of 18 U.S.C. § 911. These allegations constitute federal felony offenses and are being handled through the federal judicial process.”
Officials also addressed additional concerns, stating, “ICE also addressed inaccurate information circulating on social media regarding the operation. According to ICE, no shots were fired by ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations personnel during the operation, nor did ICE witness officers with the West Monroe Police Department discharge a firearm during the initial vehicle stop.”
They also stated that the efforts of ICE agents were not directed at restaurants or businesses, as has been suggested on social media. ICE stated that agents were present at one business location solely to locate two absconded crew members.
Sheriff Marc Mashaw emphasized the importance of interagency cooperation in protecting the community.
“The Ouachita Parish Sheriff’s Office remains committed to working alongside our local, state, and federal law enforcement partners to protect the citizens of Ouachita Parish. These operations are focused on individuals who have violated immigration laws and, in many cases, have demonstrated a disregard for the law through serious criminal activity. We also believe transparency is essential. When questions or allegations arise, they should be thoroughly reviewed so the public receives accurate information based on facts, not speculation. I also caution the public against accepting information from social media influencers who may have hidden agendas aimed at creating chaos and confusion among our citizens.”
Officials with the department concluded by stating, “The Ouachita Parish Sheriff’s Office appreciates its continued partnership with ICE and other law enforcement agencies and remains committed to public safety, accountability, and providing accurate information to the community.”
